title: Funding-Route Uplift: How a Duplicate Domain Charge Was Paid and Refunded
content:
> Harborline Customer Accounts. Reads the duplicate's payment method and refund destination on the Domain Registrations billing history, and the account's credit ledger.

**Clause.** The funding-route uplift of the duplicate-charge goodwill follows how the duplicate was paid and where its refund line sent the money: a duplicate taken from a card or PayPal and refunded to that original payment method, which reaches the customer only after the card or PayPal processing time, adds $4.00; a duplicate taken from a card or PayPal and refunded to account credit at the customer's election, its refund credit entry for the duplicate's order number being on the account's credit ledger, adds $3.00; any other duplicate, such as one paid from account credit and so refunded to account credit, adds nothing. The uplift is a fixed sum added to the duplicate-charge goodwill figure.

| Duplicate paid by | Refund line sent the money to | Refund credit entry for the duplicate's order number on the credit ledger | Uplift |
|---|---|---|---|
| card or PayPal | the original payment method | not required | $4.00 |
| card or PayPal | account credit | present | $3.00 |
| card or PayPal | account credit | absent | nothing |
| account credit | account credit | either | nothing |
